## Step 2: Making the scraper dynamic

### 1. Turning the scraper into a function 

* a. Pseudo-Code
A: Define a function that takes a starting year and month as inputs

B: If the year is earlier than 2013, print a message and exit the function

C: Initialize an empty list to store enforcement actions

D: Start from page 1 and loop through pages using a while loop

E: For each page:

    1. Construct the URL with the page number

    2. Request the webpage and parse the HTML

    3. Extract title, date, category, and link for each enforcement action

    4. Append results to the list

    5. Check the oldest date on the page

    6. If the date is earlier than the starting date, stop looping

    7. Pause for 1 second before requesting the next page

F: Convert the collected data into a dataframe

G: Save the dataframe as a CSV file and return it


* b. Create Dynamic Scraper
def scrape_enforcement_actions(start_year, start_month, RUN_SCRAPER=False):
    """
    Scrape HHS OIG enforcement actions from a given start year/month to today.
    Step 2b version: does NOT save CSV yet.
    """

    # ---- 安全开关 ----
    if not RUN_SCRAPER:
        print("RUN_SCRAPER is False. Skipping web scraping.")
        return None

    # ---- 年份检查 ----
    if start_year < 2013:
        print("Error: Enforcement Actions are only available from 2013 onward.")
        return None

    base_url = "https://oig.hhs.gov"
    data = []

    start_date = datetime(start_year, start_month, 1)

    page = 1
    keep_scraping = True

    while keep_scraping:
        print(f"Scraping page {page}...")

        url = f"https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/?page={page}"
        response = requests.get(url)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "lxml")

        cards = soup.find_all("li", class_="usa-card")

        if len(cards) == 0:
            break

        for card in cards:
            a_tag = card.find("h2").find("a")
            title = a_tag.text.strip()
            link = base_url + a_tag["href"]

            date_str = card.find("span").text.strip()
            date = datetime.strptime(date_str, "%B %d, %Y")

            categories = card.find_all("li", class_="usa-tag")
            category = categories[0].text.strip() if categories else None

            # ---- 停止条件 ----
            if date < start_date:
                keep_scraping = False
                break

            data.append({
                "title": title,
                "date": date,
                "category": category,
                "link": link
            })

        page += 1
        time.sleep(1)

    df = pd.DataFrame(data)
    print(f"Scraped {len(df)} enforcement actions.")
    return df

* c. Test Your Code
def scrape_enforcement_actions(start_year, start_month, RUN_SCRAPER=False):
    """
    Scrape HHS OIG enforcement actions from a given start year/month to today.
    Step 2c version: saves results to CSV.
    """

    # ---- 安全开关 ----
    if not RUN_SCRAPER:
        print("RUN_SCRAPER is False. Skipping web scraping.")
        return None

    # ---- 年份检查 ----
    if start_year < 2013:
        print("Error: Enforcement Actions are only available from 2013 onward.")
        return None

    base_url = "https://oig.hhs.gov"
    data = []

    start_date = datetime(start_year, start_month, 1)

    page = 1
    keep_scraping = True

    while keep_scraping:
        print(f"Scraping page {page}...")

        url = f"https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/?page={page}"
        response = requests.get(url)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "lxml")

        cards = soup.find_all("li", class_="usa-card")

        if len(cards) == 0:
            break

        for card in cards:
            a_tag = card.find("h2").find("a")
            title = a_tag.text.strip()
            link = base_url + a_tag["href"]

            date_str = card.find("span").text.strip()
            date = datetime.strptime(date_str, "%B %d, %Y")

            categories = card.find_all("li", class_="usa-tag")
            category = categories[0].text.strip() if categories else None

            # ---- 停止条件 ----
            if date < start_date:
                keep_scraping = False
                break

            data.append({
                "title": title,
                "date": date,
                "category": category,
                "link": link
            })

        page += 1
        time.sleep(1)

    df = pd.DataFrame(data)

    filename = f"enforcement_actions_{start_year}_{start_month}.csv"
    df.to_csv(filename, index=False)

    print(f"Saved {len(df)} rows to {filename}")
    return df

### 1. Plot the number of enforcement actions over time

```{python}
monthly_total = (
    df.groupby("year_month")
      .size()
      .reset_index(name="count")
)

chart_total = (
    alt.Chart(monthly_total)
    .mark_line(point=True)
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month"),
        y=alt.Y("count:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),
        tooltip=["year_month:T", "count:Q"]
    )
    .properties(
        title="Monthly Enforcement Actions (Since Jan 2022)",
        width=650,
        height=400
    )
)
```

def classify_criminal_action(title):
    t = title.lower()

    if any(k in t for k in ["medicare", "medicaid", "health care", "healthcare"]):
        return "Health Care Fraud"

    elif any(k in t for k in ["bank", "wire fraud", "launder", "financial"]):
        return "Financial Fraud"

    elif any(k in t for k in ["drug", "opioid", "controlled substance"]):
        return "Drug Enforcement"

    elif any(k in t for k in ["bribery", "kickback", "corruption"]):
        return "Bribery / Corruption"

    else:
        return "Other"


df_criminal = df[df["category"] == "Criminal and Civil Actions"].copy()

df_criminal["subtype"] = df_criminal["title"].apply(classify_criminal_action)

df_criminal["subtype"].value_counts()

# Combine
monthly_criminal = (
    df_criminal
    .groupby(["year_month", "subtype"])
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="count")
)

monthly_criminal.head()

chart_criminal = (
    alt.Chart(monthly_criminal)
    .mark_line(point=True)
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month"),
        y=alt.Y("count:Q", title="Number of Actions"),
        color=alt.Color("subtype:N", title="Criminal Action Type"),
        tooltip=["year_month:T", "subtype:N", "count:Q"]
    )
    .properties(
        title="Criminal and Civil Actions by Topic (Since Jan 2022)",
        width=650,
        height=400
    )
)

chart_criminal

* based on five topics
Figure 3 further disaggregates Criminal and Civil Actions into five topic areas—Health Care Fraud, Financial Fraud, Drug Enforcement, Bribery/Corruption, and Other—based on keyword classification of enforcement action titles. Monthly counts are plotted to illustrate trends across these subcategories over time.
